title: The target-open immersion locus of the section-ring map is stable under a square-condition action
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H\to S$ a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with an $S$-group scheme structure and connected fibres $H_s=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-connected-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means a scheme $H$ with $S$-morphisms $m:H\times_SH\to H$, $i:H\to H$, $e:S\to H$ satisfying associativity, identity and inverse identities; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation, equipped with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$, meaning that $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(g,a(h,x))=a(gh,x)$ as morphism identities. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For any $S$-scheme $B$, put $X_B=X\times_SB$, with structure map $q_B:X_B\to B$, and let $M_B$ be the tensor pullback of $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $g\in H(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)$ let $\tau_g:X_B\to X_B$ be the action $x\mapsto gx$. Say that $M$ satisfies the square condition for this action if, for every such $B$ and every $g,h\in H(B)$, there is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N.$$ All tensors are module sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is equality of the translation differences in the group of invertible-module classes modulo modules pulled back from $B$; no coherence or chosen isomorphisms are part of the condition. Assume that $M$ satisfies this square condition. Assume that the opens $X_s$, over all positive integers $n$ and sections $s\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})$, cover $X$. Let $$A=\Gamma_*(X,M)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})$$ be the graded section ring [def-sc-invertible-section-ring], let $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], and let $r:X\to P$ be the canonical morphism of [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map]. Let $P_0\subseteq P$ be the union of all open subschemes $V\subseteq P$ for which $r^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $W=r^{-1}(P_0)$. Then the image on underlying points of $H\times_SW\to X$ equals $W$. Moreover, for every quasi-compact open subscheme $T\subseteq W$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], the restriction $M|_T$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Guo, section 6.1 and Proposition 6.2(iii), printed pp.14--15 (affine-base, smooth separated finite-presentation specialization); March 31, 2026 version, read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: For a smooth affine test scheme $B\to S$ put $p:P_B\to P$, and let $Q_B$ be the union of target opens on which $r_B$ is an open immersion. The projection $p$ is smooth by the smooth clause of [lem-pc-proper-base-change]; its restrictions to source and target opens are smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Pulling back an isomorphism onto an open subscheme gives an isomorphism onto the inverse-image open: this follows immediately from [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus $p^{-1}(P_0)\subseteq Q_B$.

source.place: Tags 01VB, 01V6, 01V7 and 01UA; schemes, Tag 01JY for the elementary open-subscheme base change

proof.text: Conversely, take an open $V\subseteq P_B$ for which $r_B^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an open immersion. Its image $I=p(V)$ is open. The smooth surjection $V\to I$ is an fpqc covering in the precise sense of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: for each affine $J\subseteq I$, choose affine neighborhoods in $V\times_I J$; their images are open and cover $J$, so finitely many suffice by compactness of the affine space $J$. These neighborhoods are affine opens in $V$ and their images have union exactly $J$. Its flatness was established in step 1. The pullback of $r^{-1}(I)\to I$ along this cover is exactly $r_B^{-1}(V)\to V$. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-open-immersion] to conclude that $I\subseteq P_0$. Hence $V\subseteq p^{-1}(P_0)$. Taking the union gives $Q_B=p^{-1}(P_0)$ and $r_B^{-1}(Q_B)=W\times_S B$.

source.place: Tag 02L3, applied with the covering of Topologies Tag 022B; smooth maps are open by the cited step-1 tools

proof.text: Fix such a $B$ and $g\in H(B)$. Apply [lem-sfb-square-action-proj-translation-extension], whose group, square-condition, and generation hypotheses are precisely those of the item, to obtain $\sigma_g:U_g\simeq U^{\prime}_g$ with $\sigma_g r_B=r_B\tau_g$. If $V\subseteq P_B$ is an admissible open in the definition of $Q_B$, replace it by $V\cap U_g$, which has the same inverse image under $r_B$. For $V\prime=\sigma_g(V\cap U_g)$ we have $r_B^{-1}(V\prime)=\tau_g(r_B^{-1}(V))$: use the displayed identity and its inverse, and that both $U_g$ and $U^{\prime}_g$ contain $r_B(X_B)$. The induced map on these inverse images is conjugate by the isomorphisms $\tau_g$ and $\sigma_g$ to the given open immersion. By the definition of open immersion it is an open immersion. Thus $\tau_g(r_B^{-1}(Q_B))\subseteq r_B^{-1}(Q_B)$. Repeating for $g^{-1}$ gives equality.

source.place: Proposition 6.2, first assertion and implication to (iii); transport of target opens written out

proof.text: Cover $H$ by affine opens $B$. Each $B\to S$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Take $g\in H(B)$ to be the inclusion $B\to H$, the universal element over this chart. Steps 2--3 say that its translation preserves $W\times_S B$. The action on $B\times_S W$ therefore has image in $W$. These charts cover $H\times_S W$, proving that the entire action has image in $W$. The unit map $w\mapsto(e(q(w)),w)$ maps back to $w$, proving the reverse inclusion. Consequently $H\cdot W=W$ on points. This argument uses universal sections on smooth test bases, so it does not assume that rational points over residue fields exhaust an orbit.

source.place: Proposition 6.2(iii), saturation; universal-element argument on affine opens of H

proof.text: The restrictions $r^{-1}(V)\to V$ for the opens defining $P_0$ identify their sources with open subschemes. These identifications agree on overlaps because they are restrictions of the same map $r$; equivalently their local inverses agree wherever both are defined. They glue to identify $W$ with an open subscheme of $P_0$, hence of $P$. For a quasi-compact open $T\subseteq W$, its image $U=r(T)$ is therefore a quasi-compact open of $P$ and $r_T:T\xrightarrow{\sim}U$. Quasi-compactness here is preserved by this homeomorphism. This is just the open-subscheme characterization in [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tags 01HE and 01IO; gluing inverse maps on target-open charts

proof.text: Restrict sections to $T$ to obtain the graded map $\psi:A\to\Gamma_*(T,M|_T)$. The original nonvanishing opens still cover $T$. The inverse images of $D_+(s)$ and fraction maps for $r|_T$ are the restrictions of those in [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map], so this is exactly the canonical map for $\psi$. Since $T$ is quasi-compact, [lem-trf-proj-canonical-map-twist-comparison] gives $d\geq1$ and, for every $k\geq1$, $(r|_T)^*\mathcal O_P(dk)\simeq(M|_T)^{\otimes dk}$. Since $U$ is quasi-compact, [lem-trf-proj-qc-open-twist-ample] gives $e\geq1$ such that every $\mathcal O_U(ek)$ is invertible and ample. Choose the common multiple $m=de$ to obtain both the comparison in degree $m$ and ampleness of $\mathcal O_U(m)$.

source.place: Tags 01NK and 01N8 (canonical graded comparison); Tag 01MW (ample positive twists on a quasi-compact Proj open)

proof.text: Transporting the affine nonvanishing neighborhoods in the definition of ampleness along the scheme isomorphism $r_T:T\simeq U$ shows that $r_T^*\mathcal O_U(m)$ is ample: sections and their nonvanishing opens correspond, and affineness is invariant under an isomorphism. The degree-$m$ comparison and [lem-sc-ample-iso] imply that $(M|_T)^{\otimes m}$ is ample. For each $t\in T$, its affine nonvanishing neighborhood supplied by this ampleness is cut out by a section of $((M|_T)^{\otimes m})^{\otimes n}=(M|_T)^{\otimes mn}$ with $n\geq1$. The same section, now viewed in degree $mn\geq1$, therefore verifies condition (2) of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] for $M|_T$ itself; condition (1) is the assumed quasi-compactness of $T$. This proves absolute ampleness, including when $T$ is empty.
